title: Grateful Dead Live at Madison Square Garden on 1982-09-20
lineage: Sennheiser 421's (18th row - Center) > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassette > Playback on Nak Dragon > Sony R700 DAT deck (sbm-on) - used only as A>D converter (44.1khz) > ZA2 > CDR (x1)  > EAC(tracked with Addawav & CDWav) >SHN

ai_review.summary: Iconic early‑80s Madison Square Garden show with Jerry’s razor‑sharp playing, but plagued by a subpar recording and a missing "Touch of Grey" encore.
ai_review.review: The performance is remembered for an electrifying New York crowd, a dream‑setlist from the early ’80s and especially Jerry Garcia’s crisp guitar work and strong vocals on songs like Fire. Unfortunately the tape quality is described as a “travesty,” with inconsistent levels that make parts hard to hear, and the Touch of Grey encore is absent, which drags down the overall listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is praised (high energy, standout Jerry performance) while recording quality is criticized (poor/muddy sound and missing encore), leading to a moderate combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers call the recording a travesty, noting inconsistent levels, occasional muffled sections, and the omission of the Touch of Grey encore.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑80s setlist described as a 'wish list' and highly desirable, with strong momentum throughout the show.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for crisp, sharp guitar work and fantastic vocals; highlighted on Fire.
